newsitem.title: BELARUS: OLYMPICS-BELARUS LEADER URGES MORE SPORT, LESS VODKA.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-BELARUS LEADER URGES MORE SPORT, LESS VODKA.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko chided his countrymen on Sunday for their fondness for vodka and said they should follow his example and take up sport.

The 42-year-old former collective farm manager told visiting IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch that Minsk had its "sportiest government" for years, with ministers involved in soccer, tennis and skiing.
Sport, Interfax news agency quoted Lukashenko as saying, was his "favourite activity". The same could not be said of all Belarussians, though.
"People should go more often to the stadiums than to the drying out clinics and hospitals," Lukashenko said.

Last week Lukashenko, who plans a decree demanding more "discipline" in society, was reported to have sacked a string of senior officials from the city Borisov for allegedly hosting a drunken party on the day he signed a Union Treaty with Russia.
Interfax quoted him as saying that Belarussian athletes would continue to compete under their own national flag following the treaty signing.
